comparison.objective: Candidate tunes and locks an impact-energy absorber until repeated carriage stops are safe; pr-1799 squares and secures a milling vise using an indicator sweep.
comparison.physical_skill: Both involve adjustment followed by locking and measurement, but the candidate manipulates a small collar and recessed setscrew with a hex key and evaluates dynamic impacts. pr-1799 rotates a vise assembly, operates an eccentric cam, and traverses a spring-loaded indicator along a jaw.
comparison.success_condition: Candidate requires two non-bottoming cycles at at least 0.85 J and 0.3–3.30 m/s, within 12 mm stroke, with no rebound, overload, hard-stop strike, or setting drift. pr-1799 requires a complete ±30 mm indicator sweep, at most 0.20 mm span for higher credit, clamp compression, and stable secured alignment.
comparison.reason: This is the closest record because both test iterative adjustment, verification, and locking. The decisive measured ability differs: shaping dynamic stopping behavior through a retained damping setting versus minimizing static geometric alignment error through contact metrology. Candidate rubric still omits numeric rebound, overload, drift, torque, and damage thresholds.
